text:
ConocoPhillips fell 2.9% today as crude oil prices slipped below $90 a barrel—US oil dropped to $89.53—and broader energy sector momentum stalled. The company also faces headwinds from the collapse of climate negotiations over the weekend, which rejected language on phasing out fossil fuels; while this removes a near-term regulatory threat, it heightens longer-term uncertainty about energy demand and policy direction. The stock is down nearly 2% over two weeks as the initial refinery profit boom that boosted energy stocks earlier this year appears to be unwinding.

Geopolitical risks to oil supply—Iran-backed attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi strikes on Saudi refineries—have so far failed to lift prices enough to offset the sector's shift in sentiment. Without a floor from rising oil or a tailwind from refining margins, the stock is tracking with the broader energy sector's pullback.
